points.quote: Google Gemini is the University's preferred generative AI tool because any data inputted is fully protected and chats are never used for training or human review by Google. You must sign into Gemini using your University credentials to ensure this.
points.gist: Gemini is the preferred generative AI tool, with data protected and not used for training or human review, provided you sign in with University credentials.

points.quote: ‘False authorship’ refers to creating or modifying academic work, either fully or partially, using unauthorised or undisclosed help from people (eg family, proofreaders, essay mills) or technology (eg generative AI, software, machine translation) without approval or acknowledgment and to such an extent that you can no longer be considered the author of the work.
points.gist: False authorship means using unauthorised or undisclosed help from people or technology, without approval or acknowledgment, to the point you are no longer the author.

points.quote: False authorship is considered an academic misconduct offence under University policy and is treated very seriously.
points.anchor: Student guidance on using AI and translation tools
points.gist: False authorship is an academic misconduct offence under University policy and is treated very seriously.

points.quote: As always, check your assessment briefs and guidelines carefully, and if you are not sure about acceptable use, ask your teacher or coordinator.
points.gist: Check assessment briefs and guidelines carefully, and ask your teacher or coordinator if unsure about acceptable use.

points.quote: Requesting direct answers or responses: asking generative AI your assessment questions or titles, and then using the generated response in assessed work without approval or attribution.
points.anchor: Examples of poor and/or unacceptable use of generative AI in assessments
points.gist: Asking generative AI your assessment questions and using the response in assessed work without approval or attribution is poor use.

points.quote: Submitting chunks of unedited text generated by AI: submitting academic work that is partly or entirely generated using AI, without any personal review, understanding, or modification, will be deemed false authorship.
points.anchor: Examples of poor and/or unacceptable use of generative AI in assessments
points.gist: Submitting partly or wholly AI-generated work without personal review, understanding or modification will be deemed false authorship.

points.quote: Generate ideas - but not generate assessed work: AI can be used to assist you in generating ideas, but again, this should not be a shortcut for critical thinking, deeper analysis and academic writing, all of which should be your own and you should be able to explain if asked.
points.anchor: Examples of good and/or acceptable use of generative AI in assessments
points.gist: AI can help generate ideas but not replace critical thinking, analysis and writing, which should be your own and explainable.

points.quote: Enhancement beyond expectations: we expect the work you produce to reflect what we know of you from classroom participation, VLE engagement, oral tasks, homework submissions, and day-to-day interactions.
points.anchor: Examples of poor and/or unacceptable use of generative AI in assessments
points.gist: Work is expected to match what staff know of you from classroom participation, VLE engagement, oral tasks, homework and daily interactions.

points.quote: It is advisable to keep records of the work you have done and to save different copies of your work rather than overwriting the same file all the time.
points.gist: Keep records of your work and save different copies rather than overwriting the same file.

points.quote: If there is a suspicion of academic misconduct through generative AI use, you may be requested to attend a panel hearing on the case and asked to explain how you produced your work.
points.gist: If generative AI misconduct is suspected, you may have to attend a panel hearing and explain how you produced your work.

points.quote: Therefore, over reliance on machine translation to the extent that it diminishes your active involvement and understanding, and results in false authorship, is strictly prohibited.
points.anchor: Translation tools or services (human or digital)
points.gist: Over-reliance on machine translation that diminishes your involvement and understanding and results in false authorship is strictly prohibited.

points.quote: Submitting lengthy chunks of translated work: translated text which is at sentence level or beyond risks submitting work of false authorship.
points.anchor: Examples of poor and/or unacceptable use of translation services or tools in assessments
points.gist: Translated text at sentence level or beyond risks being false authorship.

points.quote: Using automated paraphrasing tools, for example, can result in work of false authorship being submitted (as well as often poor paraphrasing!) and means you are not applying the skills that you are here to learn.
points.gist: Automated paraphrasing tools can lead to false authorship and mean you are not applying the skills you are here to learn.

points.quote: be aware that misuse and over reliance on the tools and services discussed could result in a) a lower grade in comparison to the original draft; and b) being referred for academic misconduct as the submission may be considered false authorship.
points.gist: Misuse and over-reliance could mean a lower grade than the original draft and referral for academic misconduct.

points.quote: Therefore, tutors can advise on and support students with some applications but such guidance will be limited so as not to disadvantage students who may not have access to the functionality available in the premium, paid-for editions.
points.gist: Tutor guidance on applications is limited so as not to disadvantage students without access to premium, paid-for editions.
